blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Chineside

items.t: SSMUH — the rule that actually governs this sub-area's lots: Coquitlam's small-scale multi-unit housing rules allow up to 3 units on lots 280 m² or smaller and up to 4 units on lots larger than 280 m² and under 4,050 m², including secondary suites and carriage or laneway homes; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer fall outside the SSMUH rules. These units are not strata condos and do not appear in condo searches.

Coquitlam replaced its OCP in 2026. The Interim Official Community Plan was adopted April 27, 2026 (Bylaws 5511/5512, 2026), superseding the Citywide OCP Bylaw No. 3479, 2001, with a fuller OCP update anticipated to begin in 2027 — planning documents and listing copy citing the old Citywide OCP are a plan out of date.
A zero-sale month is this sub-area's documented shape.

The density story here is suites and carriage homes, not strata. The SSMUH framework (up to 3 units on lots ≤280 m², up to 4 units under 4,050 m²) is the only multi-unit mechanism operating on Chineside streets — which is why a sub-area can be densifying and still have zero condos.

The "Harbour" name search lands in another city. Harbour Place Estates (1872 Harbour Street) is a Port Coquitlam townhouse complex that name-based searches attach to the Chines area; it has no connection to Chineside beyond a shared word.
No Chineside school catchment is verified yet.

items.t: Coquitlam property taxes: payment was due July 2, 2026 for the January 1 – December 31, 2026 year, with a 5% penalty on any unpaid balance of current taxes after July 2, 2026 and an additional 5% penalty on any unpaid balance after September 15, 2026 (including unclaimed Home Owner Grants). Chineside is in Coquitlam, not Chilliwack, and the difference changes real deal terms. Coquitlam is on the GVR board with its own plan and tax dates; a Chilliwack filing would use a different board (CADREB), a different plan and different tax dates.

Established house lots: detached houses on the central-Coquitlam slope under the small-scale residential zones R-1, R-2 and R-3 in Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996. Lot character, only: subdivision minimums are 650 m² with 18.5 m width in R-1 and R-3, and 465 m² with 12.5 m width in R-2. These are zone minimums, not a statement about any existing lot; the zone and dimensions of a specific lot should be checked parcel by parcel. A fee-simple lot has no strata, no Form B and no strata fees.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Coquitlam utility charges cover water, sewer and drainage and solid waste; lots not connected to municipal water or sewer are outside the SSMUH rules, so property-level septic or well status is not verified — confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Chineside

items.t: Watercourse Development Permit: within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse in this part of Coquitlam a Watercourse Protection Development Permit can be required.

Bare-land strata block (for the form — no Chineside bare-land strata plan is verified): Form B diligence (provided within 7 days, max $35 + 25¢/page); depreciation reports on a 5-year cycle for stratas with 5+ lots since July 1, 2024; minimum 10% CRF contribution since November 1, 2023; rental-restriction bylaws void since November 24, 2022 (short-term restrictions may still apply by bylaw); only 55+ age bylaws valid under SPA ss.123.1/123.2, with May 1, 2023 exemptions; a listing's "45+" line is not a valid BC age bylaw.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Chineside ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31).

Chineside is in the City of Coquitlam, not Port Coquitlam; it is the central-Coquitlam slope around Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue.

Chineside and Harbour Chines are two separate board sub-areas, both in Coquitlam, sharing the "Chines" name; Harbour Chines adjoins it, with Central Coquitlam east, Ranch Park and Maillardville south, and Burquitlam west.
The named public buildings on its streets are schools and parks rather than strata complexes — Como Lake Middle School is at 1121 King Albert Avenue, on the Como Lake Avenue side.

The slope rule here is the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area: a permit can be required within 30 metres of the top of bank or top of ravine bank of any watercourse, with Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 sections 519 and 523 setting flood and riparian setbacks.

items.t: Mundy Park, 641 Hillcrest Street, is Coquitlam's largest park at 176 hectares in City descriptions, with Mundy Lake and Lost Lake, trails, sports fields, an outdoor pool and a disc golf area south-west of the Chineside slope.
Como Lake Park and Mundy Park are the two City park names recorded for central Coquitlam in City records used by this area.
The nearest Evergreen Extension (Millennium Line) station is Burquitlam, west of the sub-area, with Coquitlam Central to the east.
Coquitlam Public Library's Poirier branch at 575 Poirier Street is the south-side branch serving central Coquitlam, alongside the City Centre branch at 1169 Pinetree Way.
Eagle Ridge Hospital, 475 Guildford Way, Port Moody, is the Fraser Health hospital on the Port Moody / Coquitlam border serving this area.
The City-wide Official Community Plan (OCP) is the governing plan here; no Chineside neighbourhood plan was confirmed on a City page.
Coquitlam's 2026 utility bill was due March 31, 2026, covering January 1 to December 31, 2026, billed separately from property taxes.
Austin Avenue and Como Lake Avenue are the main roads through the Chineside slope, linking it east to Central Coquitlam and west toward Burquitlam station.
Check creek and ravine lots against the Watercourse Protection Development Permit Area — 30 metres from the top of bank — before assuming an addition or suite fits.
